# ipe() Games

> Four small games from ipe(): Iltonggi, Inkisle, Sunmeld and Claimball. Short rounds, few rules, no ads. None is released yet.

play.ipe.rest is the portal for the games made by ipe() (https://ipe.rest/). It collects four games in one place and links to each game's own official site. None of the four games has been released: no store page or release date exists for any of them. This portal has no accounts or ads, collects only basic visit statistics through Google Analytics, and has no terms of its own (each game's site has its own terms). It has a journal with notes on turn-based games, killing-time games and how ipe() makes games.

## The games

- [Iltonggi](https://iltonggi.ipe.rest): A short, fast, classic territory-conquest strategy game set in Korea's Three Kingdoms era. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iPhone first. Pricing: No ads, no tracking.
- [Inkisle](https://inkisle.ipe.rest): A light island-conquest strategy game for your phone: send fleets between islands and tint the sea your color. Status: In development. Platform: iOS first, Android alongside. Pricing: Planned: every round free · no ads · optional help items.
- [Sunmeld](https://sunmeld.ipe.rest): A merge duel against an AI opponent in one shared tub. Drop a stone, merge matching stones into the next stage, and score. Overflow the tub and you lose. Status: In development. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: Free to try, one purchase unlocks everything, no ads.
- [Claimball](https://claimball.ipe.rest): A casual duel against an AI rival on a notebook grid. The tile where your ball bounces becomes your land. Miss, and you lose land. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: Free to try. One purchase unlocks everything. No ads, no subscription..

## How ipe makes games

- Short rounds that fit a break: A round should end in minutes, and closing the app should never cost you.
- Few rules, deep reading: If the rules don't fit on one page, the game is asking too much.
- A quiet app: No streak nagging, no ads, no accounts, and no tracking inside the games.
- Say what's true, including what isn't: If it's not released, we say so. If we haven't checked, we say that too.
- The AI plays fair: Comebacks come from the rules, not from a secretly weakened opponent.

## Journal

RSS: https://play.ipe.rest/journal/feed.xml

- [Why turn-based games fit a break](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-01-why-turn-based-games-fit-a-break/): A break has an edge you did not choose. Turn-based games fit that shape: stopping costs nothing, there is time to think, and a round can end cleanly.
- [How ipe makes games](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-10-31-how-ipe-makes-games/): Five game design principles: short rounds, few rules, a quiet app, saying what is true, and fair opponents. How ipe's four games follow them.

## Languages

The site is available in 11 languages: English (en), Korean (ko), Japanese (ja), Chinese (Simplified) (zh), Spanish (es), Portuguese (Brazil) (pt), Indonesian (id), Russian (ru), Vietnamese (vi), French (fr), German (de). English is at the root; every other language lives under /<code>/ (for example /ko/, /ja/). English and Korean are written by ipe(); Japanese, Chinese (Simplified), Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Indonesian, Russian, Vietnamese, French, German are AI translations of the English original, marked as such on every page. The journal is written in English and Korean only.
